deep.reconstruction:
This page is the closing page of Riemann's memoir 'Zwei allgemeine Sätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten', dated Göttingen, 20 Feb 1857. It was published posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke (1876, ed. Weber/Dedekind). It contains no computations, only the statement of a consequence and an outlook.

Setting (from the previous pages). y = (y_1,...,y_n) is a system of n functions of x. Its branch points are a, b, ..., g. The monodromy substitutions are given constant matrices (A), (B), ..., (F), (G). Since a loop around all branch points is trivial, the product of all substitutions is the identity. So only p-2 of them, (A),...,(F), are arbitrary, and (G) is determined.

Normalisation (previous page). Riemann raises the exponents (by forcing leading coefficients of 𝔄^{-1}(y),... to vanish) and fixes the common constant factor. The result is that y is uniquely determined by the substitutions and the exponents in its characteristic.

The 'Satz' (previous page). If the branch point a is moved while all substitutions stay constant (an isomonodromic deformation, in modern terms), then y is also, as a function of a, a system of the same kind. Its branch values are b, c, ..., g, x, and its substitutions are composed of (A), ..., (F). A degenerate case occurs when there are fewer free constants than conditions. Then the system is treated as a special case of one with lower exponents, in which certain initial coefficients of the series for 𝔄^{-1}(y), 𝔅^{-1}(y), ..., 𝔊^{-1}(y) vanish. That clause ends at the top of this page.

Consequence on this page. The y_i are functions of the p variables a, b, ..., g, x. These are the p-1 branch points plus x. Continue analytically along any closed path in this p-dimensional configuration space, i.e. let all variables return to their original values. Then y either returns to itself or undergoes y -> M y. Here M is a constant matrix composed somehow ('irgendwie zusammengesetzt') from (A), ..., (F), i.e. M lies in the monodromy group they generate.

In modern terms (my gloss): the isomonodromic family is a locally constant system over the configuration space of distinct points. Its monodromy lies in the group <A,...,F>, because moving branch points around each other acts on the generators by braid-type conjugations within that group.

Outlook. Riemann forgoes a further study of these functions of several variables and of their use for integrating linear ODEs. He remarks on a special case. An integral of an algebraic function, w = ∫ R(x,s) dx with y_1 = w, y_2 = 1, is such a system with unipotent substitutions w -> w + period. Applying this principle to such an integral leads to the functions that represent the general Θ-series with arbitrary period moduli. These are viewed as functions of the branch points, i.e. the moduli.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.

The claim that the composite substitutions are 'irgendwie zusammengesetzt' from (A),...,(F) is correct but not justified here. Justification needs the braid-group action on the monodromy representation.

The well-definedness of the deformation rests on the previous page's argument. That argument carries a faint marginal note on the previous page, 'das hier ist nicht richtig [?]' ('this here is not right [?]'). The genericity/degenerate-case discussion is heuristic.

The final remark about Θ-series with arbitrary period moduli is only a sketch. For genus > 3, periods of abelian integrals give only Jacobian period matrices (the Schottky problem), not arbitrary symmetric period matrices. So the claim is at best ambiguous as stated.

results.what: Solutions of a Fuchsian system with prescribed constant monodromy, deformed in the branch points, are multivalued functions of all p variables (a,...,g,x) whose monodromy lies in the group generated by the given substitutions.
results.modern_name: Isomonodromic deformation; monodromy of an isomonodromic family over configuration space (braid group action)
results.usually_credited_to: Schlesinger (1905/1912), Fuchs (R. Fuchs 1905, Painlevé VI); conceptually Riemann 1857 (published 1876)

results.what: Abelian integrals as a special case of such systems; the principle leads to theta functions with general period moduli
results.modern_name: Variation of periods / Gauss-Manin-type viewpoint; theta functions as functions of moduli
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (this memoir, Werke 1876); later Fuchs, Schottky

deep.surprise_reason: This is the known last page of Riemann's 1857 memoir on linear ODEs with algebraic coefficients. It was published in his Werke (1876), and its isomonodromy idea is already widely credited to Riemann as the precursor of Schlesinger's work. The manuscript adds nothing beyond the published text apart from the date and handwriting.

checkable.sympy: w1,w2=symbols('w1 w2'); M=lambda w: Matrix([[1,w],[0,1]]); simplify(M(w1)*M(w2)-M(w1+w2))==zeros(2)
checkable.asserts: Monodromy substitutions of an abelian integral system (y1=integral, y2=1) compose additively: loops add periods. This is the 'special case' in the final remark.
The last substitution is determined by the others via the product relation, so only p-2 systems are arbitrary.
A braid move (A,B)->(A B A^-1, A) preserves the product and stays within the group generated by A,B. Illustrates 'irgendwie zusammengesetzt'.

transcription_corrections: First line: '(B)(y), ..., (D)(y)' should read '𝔅^{-1}(y), ..., 𝔊^{-1}(y) verschwinden'. These are Fraktur letters with exponent -1, continuing '𝔄^{-1}(y)' from the previous page. The last letter is the Fraktur G, which resembles D in the hand.
'Principes' — the manuscript appears to read 'dieses Principes' (consistent with the published Werke text); no substantive change.
